question: A confidence interval to estimate the population mean will be more precise when:

options.opb: The greater the dispersion of the sample.
options.opd: The greater the level of trust.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lower confidence level" -> "narrower confidence interval" -> "more precise estimate" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Greater dispersion of the sample" -> "wider confidence interval" -> "less precise estimate" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Smaller sample size" -> "wider confidence interval" -> "less precise estimate" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Greater level of trust" -> "unclear impact on precision" -> "possible misunderstanding of 'trust'" -> 50%
analysis: A confidence interval becomes more precise (narrower) when the confidence level is lower, as this reduces the range of values within which the population mean is estimated to lie. A lower confidence level means that we are less certain that the interval contains the true population mean, but the interval itself is narrower. In contrast, greater dispersion of the sample and smaller sample sizes lead to wider confidence intervals, reducing precision.
